args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The release had also been unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. I rolled the service back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy on v2.3.0 in all regions and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and find out why it was promoted to production when the staging RC was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **The bad release:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. It's now running in all three regions. Afterwards the service reports healthy and the error rate is down to 0.2%. Because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production, the rollback didn't need change-manager approval.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure and the rollback. It also lists two follow-ups:
  - Find out why v2.3.1 failed.
  - Find out how it reached production, since its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
